question: Does the AMCP+Kafka bee mesh control plane (hosts, inbox shards, heartbeats, reassignment) sustain 1000 simulated bees on one VM?
metrics: registration_s: seconds from last bee JVM start until both hosts report N live bees (status --wait-bees N)
submitted, replied, lost (no reply within 30 s after the end of the load), duplicates (more than one reply for a taskId)
e2e_ms p50/p95/p99 (replyMs - submitMs) over all tasks
overhead_ms p50/p95/p99 (e2e_ms - serviceMs) over tasks not affected by the kill (no attempt routed to a killed bee)
killed_bees (count of bees stopped by the in-process kill), killed_assigned_tasks (tasks whose first attempt was on a killed bee), killed_assigned_ok (of those, answered ok=true after reassignment)
peak RSS per process from /proc/<pid>/status VmHWM (2 hosts, 4 bee JVMs, Kafka broker, loadgen)
live bee count reported by each host at 60 s after the last bee JVM start

acceptance_at_1000.A1: all 1000 bees counted live by both hosts within 60 s of the last bee JVM start
acceptance_at_1000.A2: at 200 tasks/s for 120 s: 0 lost tasks (every submitted task gets exactly one reply), 0 duplicate replies, p95 control-plane overhead (e2e minus bee service time) <= 250 ms and p99 <= 1000 ms over tasks not affected by the kill
acceptance_at_1000.A3: after killing 10% of bees at t=60 s: >= 99% of tasks assigned to killed bees are answered OK after reassignment
acceptance_at_1000.A4: no OOM; every JVM within its -Xmx; Kafka heap 512 MB

notes: Simulated bees on ONE VM: this measures the control plane, not GPUs, WAN or real model latency. Thresholds are fixed now; any harness change after a run goes in an amendment file written before re-running; thresholds never change. This prereg file is never edited after registration. Stage 1 of the pipeline runs smoke (N=40, 30 s) only; N=100, 300 and 1000 are run by the next stage.
